newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing sees German economy in continued uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Issing sees German economy in continued uptrend.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing said on Thursday that he expected the German economy to continue its upward trend.
He also expects the Bundesbank to decide this year to eliminate a minimum reserve requirement on the central bank's securities repurchase agreements (repos).

"I don't think the reasonable liberation of repos will endanger the conditions of monetary policies," he said during a discussion at Nuremberg university. Issing added the economy was in an upturn, although one recently pessimistic report by the Ifo research institute appeared to be an abberation.
"All the other data are signalling that the economy is moving ahead," Issing said.
He added that it was likely the European economic monetary union (EMU) would start on schedule in January 1999.
The probability that EMU starts on January 1, 1999 is very high," he said.
